title: Four SELECTs on the message table
problem: queries.py has four empty SQL strings. Write each SELECT so the tests, which run it with ? parameters against the sample messaging data in chatdb.py, get exactly the expected rows in exactly the expected order.
requirements: Edit only queries.py; chatdb.py is the shared sample database
UNEDITED_BY_SENDER: columns id, body; messages from one sender whose edited_at is NULL; ordered by id
LATEST_IN_CHAT: columns id, sent_at; the n newest messages in one chat; equal sent_at broken by the higher id first
IN_CHAT_FROM_EITHER: column id; messages in one chat whose sender is either of two users; ordered by id
USERS_PAGE: column username; alphabetical; page size and number of rows to skip come from the parameters
Use ? placeholders for every value, in the order given in the comments
contract: Each constant is one SELECT statement as a str. Parameters: UNEDITED_BY_SENDER (sender_id,), LATEST_IN_CHAT (chat_id, n), IN_CHAT_FROM_EITHER (chat_id, user_a, user_b), USERS_PAGE (page_size, rows_to_skip)
edgeCases: A sender with no messages: empty list, not an error
Two messages with the same sent_at (tie-break needed)
n larger than the number of rows: all rows, no error
A user who also wrote in other chats (operator precedence)
A page past the last row: empty list
hints: Conceptual: each requirement maps to one clause. Which rows: WHERE. Which order: ORDER BY (with a second key for ties). How many: LIMIT/OFFSET. NULL is never equal to anything, so it needs its own operator.
Specific: edited_at needs IS NULL, not = NULL. 'Newest first, then higher id' is two ORDER BY keys, both DESC. AND binds tighter than OR, so 'this chat and (sender a or sender b)' needs parentheses.

Implementation: the shape is SELECT cols FROM messages WHERE ... ORDER BY key1 DESC, key2 DESC LIMIT ?. For the page, LIMIT ? OFFSET ? takes (page_size, rows_to_skip) in that order. Run pytest after each query, not after all four.
evaluation: Every value is a ? placeholder; no numbers or names typed into the SQL
Every query that returns more than one row has an ORDER BY that makes the order fully defined
